cards.design_implication: If designing a model to explain the slow rotation of accreting pre-main-sequence stars, include a wind braking mechanism where the wind mass loss rate is parameterized as roughly 10% of the accretion rate.
does_not_establish: The exact physical origin or driving mechanism of the wind beyond the stated rate requirement.
Empirical confirmation of the 10% ratio in all pre-main-sequence stars.
The specific statistical methods or error margins associated with the comparison.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We find that the wind alone can counteract the spin-up torque from mass accretion, solving the mystery of why accreting pre-main-sequence stars are observed to spin at less than 10% of breakup speed, provided that the mass outflow rate in the stellar winds is ~10% of the accretion rate.
limitations: The claim is conditional on the wind mass outflow rate being approximately 10% of the accretion rate.
The excerpt states a finding within a comparative analysis but does not detail the specific simulation or analytical method used to derive this ratio.
cards.statement: Wind-induced torques can counteract the spin-up torque from mass accretion in pre-main-sequence stars, provided the wind mass outflow rate is approximately 10% of the accretion rate.

cards.design_implication: When setting boundary conditions for models of classical T Tauri stars, constrain the relevant efficiency factor to the range of 'a few' to 'a few tens' of percent.
does_not_establish: A precise numerical upper or lower bound for the efficiency factor.
The applicability of these parameters to stellar types other than classical T Tauri stars.
cards.evidence_excerpt: For observationally constrained typical parameters of classical T Tauri stars, needs to be between a few and a few tens of percent.
limitations: The excerpt uses vague quantitative terms ('a few', 'a few tens') rather than precise numerical boundaries.
The specific variable referred to by 'needs to be' is not explicitly named in the excerpt, though contextually linked to wind driving efficiency.
cards.statement: For observationally constrained typical parameters of classical T Tauri stars, the efficiency factor needs to be between a few and a few tens of percent.
